discovery: Discovery of the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect (fractional Chern insulators at zero magnetic field) in moire transition-metal dichalcogenides
subfield: Condensed matter physics (topological quantum matter, moire materials)
motivation: For forty years, the fractional quantum Hall effect needed strong magnetic fields. In 2023, Xiaodong Xu's group and the Mak-Shan group independently showed that fractionally charged topological states form spontaneously at zero field in twisted bilayer MoTe2. Xu's team used optical sensing and fractionally quantized Hall transport; Mak and Shan used local thermodynamic measurements. In these fractional Chern insulators, interactions and band topology alone break time-reversal symmetry and produce anyonic topological order. The nominees built this through a decade of pioneering work on valley physics, excitons and correlated states in two-dimensional semiconductors, which turned van der Waals moire devices into a controllable platform for quantum matter. The result is a new field in its own right. Rapid confirmations, including in rhombohedral graphene, have already followed, and zero-field fractional states open a realistic route to non-Abelian anyons for topological quantum computation.
